name: Aldactone (Spironolactone) 100 mg Tablet
indication: Chronic heart failure (NYHA II-IV), Resistant hypertension, Ascites/oedema in liver cirrhosis, Nephrotic syndrome.
mechanismOfAction: Competitive aldosterone antagonist in distal renal tubule, promoting sodium excretion and potassium retention.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily in the morning with food. Avoid potassium supplements and potassium-rich salt substitutes.

monitoringAdvice: Serum potassium and creatinine at baseline, 1 week, 4 weeks, and every 3-6 months.

indication: Management of clinical conditions indicated for Urinary Tract Antibacterial (Antibiotic / Anti-infective).
mechanismOfAction: Bactericidal or bacteriostatic antimicrobial; inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis, protein synthesis, or DNA replication depending on subclass.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised: Susceptible bacterial infections according to Therapeutic Guidelines.
counselingAdvice: Complete the full prescribed course even if symptoms resolve earlier. Space doses evenly throughout the day. Report severe watery diarrhoea immediately.
cautionsAndContraindications: Check for penicillin or beta-lactam allergies. Dose reduce in moderate-to-severe renal impairment where indicated.
adverseEffects: Gastrointestinal upset (nausea, diarrhoea, cramping), fungal overgrowth (candidiasis), rash.
monitoringAdvice: Clinical resolution of infection, rash, renal function if extended therapy.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C (reconstituted suspensions store 2°C to 8°C in fridge).

name: Alprim (Trimethoprim) 300 mg Tablet
indication: Treatment of acute uncomplicated urinary tract infections caused by susceptible organisms.
mechanismOfAction: Reversibly inhibits bacterial dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), preventing synthesis of tetrahydrofolic acid, an essential precursor in thymidine and purine synthesis.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit for acute uncomplicated urinary tract infections.
counselingAdvice: Take ONCE DAILY AT BEDTIME with water for 3 to 7 days. Complete the full course. Drink plenty of water throughout the day.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in severe renal impairment (CrCl < 15 mL/min), megaloblastic anaemia due to folate deficiency, and pregnancy (first trimester folate antagonist). Can cause hyperkalaemia.
adverseEffects: Nausea, vomiting, pruritus, skin rash, hyperkalaemia, transient elevation of serum creatinine (due to inhibition of tubular creatinine secretion).
monitoringAdvice: Electrolytes (potassium) in elderly or renal-impaired patients.

name: Amoxil (Amoxicillin (as trihydrate)) 250 mg Capsule
indication: Upper and lower respiratory tract infections (CAP, acute otitis media, sinusitis), Urinary tract infections, Dental infections, Eradication of H. pylori.
mechanismOfAction: Bactericidal beta-lactam that inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), causing bacterial cell wall lysis.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit.
counselingAdvice: Take at evenly spaced intervals throughout the day with or without food. Complete the full course even if feeling better. Contact doctor if a severe skin rash, facial swelling, or watery diarrhoea develops.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in true penicillin anaphylaxis/hypersensitivity. Causes non-allergic maculopapular rash in infectious mononucleosis (glandular fever).
adverseEffects: Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, skin rash, oral or vaginal candidiasis.
monitoringAdvice: Assess clinical resolution at 48-72 hours. Check for antibiotic-associated diarrhoea (C. difficile).
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in a dry place.

name: Anginine (Glyceryl trinitrate (GTN)) 600mcg Sublingual tablet
indication: Acute relief of angina pectoris and prophylactic prevention before physical exertion.
mechanismOfAction: Converted to nitric oxide (NO) which activates guanylyl cyclase, generating cGMP and causing venous and coronary vasodilation, reducing cardiac preload and oxygen demand.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised: Acute relief and prophylaxis of angina pectoris.
counselingAdvice: Dissolve under tongue at the onset of chest pain while sitting down. If pain persists after 5 minutes, dissolve a second tablet. If pain persists after 10 minutes, dial 000 immediately.
cautionsAndContraindications: ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED with PDE5 inhibitors (Viagra, Cialis) due to fatal refractory hypotension.
adverseEffects: Throbbing headache, flushing, orthostatic hypotension, reflex tachycardia.
monitoringAdvice: Symptom frequency and relief time; review expiry date (discard bottle 3 months after opening).
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in original amber glass bottle with screw cap tightly closed.
defaultFrequency: Sublingually as needed for chest pain
defaultDirections: Dissolve ONE tablet under the tongue while sitting down at onset of chest pain. Call 000 if pain persists past 10 minutes.

commonDoses.directions: Dissolve 1 tablet under the tongue at onset of pain. Repeat once after 5 min if needed.

name: Anoro Ellipta (Umeclidinium / Vilanterol) 62.5mcg / 25mcg Dry powder inhaler
indication: Once-daily maintenance treatment to relieve symptoms in adult patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD).
mechanismOfAction: Combines umeclidinium (long-acting muscarinic antagonist blocking M3 receptors) and vilanterol (long-acting beta-2 agonist stimulating airway relaxation).
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Restricted: Maintenance bronchodilator therapy to relieve symptoms in adult patients with COPD.
counselingAdvice: Inhale ONE blister dose once daily at the same time. Open cover until click is heard, inhale deeply, hold breath for 3-4 seconds.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in narrow-angle glaucoma and severe urinary retention. Not for acute rescue.
adverseEffects: Upper respiratory tract infection, dry mouth, urinary tract infection, cough, tachycardia.
monitoringAdvice: FEV1, symptom scores (mMRC/CAT), intraocular pressure in glaucoma.
storageAdvice: Store below 30°C. Discard 6 weeks after opening moisture tray.
defaultDirections: Inhale ONE dose once daily at the same time each day.

commonDoses.directions: Inhale 1 dose daily at the same time.

indication: Management of clinical conditions indicated for ARB (Sartan) (Cardiovascular).
mechanismOfAction: Selectively blocks Angiotensin II Type 1 (AT1) receptors, producing vasodilation and reducing aldosterone secretion without inhibiting bradykinin breakdown.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for hypertension and reduction of cardiovascular/renal morbidity.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily with or without food. Rise slowly from sitting or lying down to prevent lightheadedness.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in bilateral renal artery stenosis and pregnancy. Avoid combining with ACE inhibitors.
adverseEffects: Dizziness, headache, hyperkalaemia, hypotension, mild fatigue.
monitoringAdvice: Baseline and periodic EUC (serum potassium, creatinine, eGFR) after starting or escalating dose.

name: Atacand (Candesartan cilexetil) 16 mg Tablet
indication: Hypertension, Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) as add-on or when ACEi not tolerated.
mechanismOfAction: Prodrug hydrolysed to candesartan, selectively blocking the binding of angiotensin II to AT1 receptors, preventing vasoconstriction and aldosterone release.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit for hypertension and heart failure.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily with or without food at the same time each day. Very low incidence of cough compared to ACE inhibitors.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in pregnancy. Caution with potassium-sparing diuretics. Monitor renal function in volume depletion.
adverseEffects: Dizziness, headache, back pain, hyperkalaemia, hypotension.
monitoringAdvice: BP, serum potassium, and renal function at baseline and after titration.

defaultDirections: Take ONE tablet ONCE daily in the evening

commonDoses.directions: Take ONE tablet ONCE daily in the evening

indication: Management of clinical conditions indicated for Statin + Cholesterol Inhibitor (Cardiovascular).
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis, increasing hepatic LDL receptor density and LDL clearance.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for hypercholesterolaemia or high cardiovascular disease risk score.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily, with or without food. Statins with short half-lives (simvastatin, pravastatin) are best taken in the evening. Promptly report any unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or brown urine.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in active liver disease or unexplained persistent transaminase elevations. Caution in elderly, high alcohol intake, and renal impairment.
adverseEffects: Myalgia, mild gastrointestinal upset, transient transaminase elevation. Rare: rhabdomyolysis, autoimmune necrotizing myopathy.
monitoringAdvice: Baseline LFTs, lipid profile at 6-12 weeks post-initiation or dose change, baseline CK (repeat if muscle symptoms develop).
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C or 30°C in original container protected from moisture.

name: Avanza (Mirtazapine) 15 mg Film-coated Tablet
indication: Major depressive episodes, especially with prominent insomnia, anxiety, or anorexia/weight loss.
mechanismOfAction: Antagonises central presynaptic alpha-2 auto- and hetero-receptors, increasing noradrenergic and serotonergic transmission; blocks 5-HT2 and 5-HT3 receptors and potently blocks H1 receptors.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit for Major Depressive Disorder.
counselingAdvice: Take ONCE DAILY AT BEDTIME due to marked sedative effect. Increases appetite and can cause significant weight gain. Swallow with liquid.
cautionsAndContraindications: Sedation is paradoxically more pronounced at lower doses (15mg) than higher doses (30-45mg) due to increasing noradrenergic activation. Bone marrow suppression (rare agranulocytosis)—report fever/sore throat.
adverseEffects: Marked somnolence, increased appetite, weight gain, dry mouth, constipation, dizziness, peripheral oedema.
monitoringAdvice: Body weight, FBC if signs of infection occur (fever, sore throat, stomatitis).

indication: Management of clinical conditions indicated for ICS + LABA (Respiratory).
mechanismOfAction: Dual-action inhaler combining an inhaled corticosteroid (ICS; reduces airway inflammation) and a long-acting beta-2 agonist (LABA; provides sustained bronchodilation).
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Restricted: Maintenance treatment of asthma or severe COPD frequent exacerbators.
counselingAdvice: Rinse mouth and gargle with water, then spit out after inhalation to prevent oral thrush and hoarseness. Use daily for maintenance even when feeling well.
cautionsAndContraindications: Not for acute monotherapy in life-threatening asthma exacerbations unless on an approved SMART/MART protocol with formoterol.
adverseEffects: Oral candidiasis (thrush), dysphonia (hoarse voice), tremor, palpitations, cough.
monitoringAdvice: Peak expiratory flow / spirometry, inhaler technique check, symptom control scores (ACQ/ACT).
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C or 30°C in dry place.

name: Brintellix (Vortioxetine (as hydrobromide)) 10mg Film-coated tablet
indication: Treatment of major depressive episodes in adults.
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits 5-HT reuptake, acts as 5-HT3, 5-HT1D, and 5-HT7 antagonist, 5-HT1B partial agonist, and 5-HT1A agonist, enhancing multiple monoaminergic neurotransmitter networks.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Restricted: Major depressive disorder in patients who have failed or not tolerated another antidepressant.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily with or without food. Takes 2 to 4 weeks for full mood benefits. Generally lower rates of sexual dysfunction and weight gain compared to SSRIs.

adverseEffects: Nausea (very common initially, usually resolves within 2 weeks), headache, abnormal dreams, pruritus.
monitoringAdvice: Clinical depression response, suicide risk early in therapy, nausea management.

name: Chlorsig (Chloramphenicol) 0.5% (5 mg / mL, 10 mL) Ophthalmic Eye Drops Solution
indication: Treatment of bacterial conjunctivitis and other superficial ocular infections caused by susceptible organisms.
mechanismOfAction: Broad-spectrum bacteriostatic antibiotic that reversibly binds to the 50S subunit of bacterial ribosomes, inhibiting peptidyl transferase and peptide bond formation.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit for superficial eye infections.
counselingAdvice: Instill ONE to TWO drops into the affected eye(s) every 2 to 4 hours for the first 48 hours, then reduce frequency to 4 times daily. Continue for 48 hours after the eye appears normal. Store in refrigerator (2-8°C); protect from light. Discard 28 days after opening bottle. Do NOT wear contact lenses during infection or treatment.
cautionsAndContraindications: Hypersensitivity to chloramphenicol. Extremely rare case reports of aplastic anaemia with topical ophthalmic use. Do not use for longer than 7 days without medical review.
adverseEffects: Transient mild stinging or burning sensation on instillation, minor allergic conjunctivitis.
monitoringAdvice: Clinical resolution at 48 hours. If symptoms worsen, review for corneal involvement.
storageAdvice: Store in a refrigerator (2°C to 8°C). Protect from light. Discard 28 days after opening.

indication: Management of clinical conditions indicated for Anti-gout agent (Rheumatology / Gout).

pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for chronic hyperuricaemia and recurrent gouty arthritis.

name: Colgout (Colchicine) 500 mcg Tablet
indication: Treatment of acute gouty arthritis, Prophylaxis against gout flares during initiation of allopurinol/urate-lowering therapy.
mechanismOfAction: Binds to tubulin dimers, preventing microtubule assembly, thereby inhibiting neutrophil chemotaxis, adhesion, and phagocytosis of monosodium urate crystals.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit for acute gout and gout prophylaxis.
counselingAdvice: For acute gout: Take ONE tablet (500mcg) at the first sign of flare, followed by ONE tablet 1 hour later. Maximum 2 to 3 tablets (1.5mg) per acute attack. Cease immediately if diarrhoea or vomiting develops. For flare prevention: Take ONE tablet daily or twice daily.
cautionsAndContraindications: Narrow therapeutic index. High toxicity with overdose. Contraindicated in severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min) or severe hepatic impairment when co-prescribed with strong P-gp or CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, erythromycin, cyclosporin, verapamil).
adverseEffects: Diarrhoea (frequent sign of toxicity), nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramping. High doses: Bone marrow suppression, rhabdomyolysis, myopathy.
monitoringAdvice: Renal function (eGFR), monitor for GI toxicity (diarrhoea).

name: Coversyl (Perindopril arginine) 10 mg Film-coated Tablet
indication: Hypertension, Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, Reduction of risk of cardiac events in stable coronary artery disease.
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE), preventing conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, causing vasodilation and decreased aldosterone secretion.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit for hypertension and reduction of cardiovascular risk.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily in the morning before breakfast. Dry persistent cough may develop (notify doctor). Rise slowly from sitting/lying positions to prevent postural dizziness.

monitoringAdvice: Check baseline U&Es and eGFR. Recheck electrolytes and creatinine within 1-2 weeks of initiation or dose escalation.
storageAdvice: Store below 30°C in tightly closed original moisture-resistant container.

indication: Management of clinical conditions indicated for Statin (Cardiovascular).
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis, increasing hepatic LDL receptor density and LDL clearance.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for hypercholesterolaemia or high cardiovascular disease risk score.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily, with or without food. Statins with short half-lives (simvastatin, pravastatin) are best taken in the evening. Promptly report any unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or brown urine.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in active liver disease or unexplained persistent transaminase elevations. Caution in elderly, high alcohol intake, and renal impairment.
adverseEffects: Myalgia, mild gastrointestinal upset, transient transaminase elevation. Rare: rhabdomyolysis, autoimmune necrotizing myopathy.
monitoringAdvice: Baseline LFTs, lipid profile at 6-12 weeks post-initiation or dose change, baseline CK (repeat if muscle symptoms develop).
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C or 30°C in original container protected from moisture.

name: Crestor (Rosuvastatin (as calcium)) 10 mg Tablet
indication: Hypercholesterolaemia, Mixed dyslipidaemia, Prevention of major cardiovascular events in high-risk patients.
mechanismOfAction: Potent competitive inhibitor of HMG-CoA reductase, producing marked reductions in plasma LDL-C and apolipoprotein B.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit (5mg, 10mg); Restricted benefit (20mg, 40mg) for patients with very high risk of CAD.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily at any time of day with or without food. Do not take antacids within 2 hours of rosuvastatin. Report any muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in active liver disease, severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min for 40mg dose), pregnancy. Start at 5mg in Asian patients due to increased plasma exposure.
adverseEffects: Common: Myalgia, headache, asthenia, abdominal pain, nausea. Rare: Proteinuria, rhabdomyolysis, hepatitis.
monitoringAdvice: Baseline lipid profile and renal function. Consider lower starting dose (5mg) in elderly or Asian ancestry.

name: Diprosone (Betamethasone dipropionate) 0.05% (500 mcg / g, 15g & 50g) Topical Cream
indication: Relief of inflammatory and pruritic manifestations of corticosteroid-responsive dermatoses (severe eczema, psoriasis, lichen planus).
mechanismOfAction: Potent synthetic fluorinated corticosteroid exerting anti-inflammatory, antipruritic, and vasoconstrictive actions by inhibiting phospholipase A2.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit for inflammatory skin conditions.
counselingAdvice: Apply sparingly to affected areas ONCE or TWICE daily and rub in gently. Use the 'Fingertip Unit' (FTU) rule. Do NOT apply to the face, groin, or axillae unless specifically instructed. Do not use under occlusion unless directed.
cautionsAndContraindications: Risk of skin atrophy (thinning), striae, telangiectasia, and systemic hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis suppression with prolonged use or large surface areas. Contraindicated in rosacea, perioral dermatitis, viral/fungal skin infections.
adverseEffects: Burning, itching, skin thinning/atrophy, striae, folliculitis, hypertrichosis.
monitoringAdvice: Reassess skin after 2-4 weeks; taper to intermittent or lower potency steroid once controlled.

name: Doryx (Doxycycline (as hyclate)) 100 mg Capsule / Tablet
indication: Respiratory tract infections (atypical pneumonia, acute exacerbation of COPD), Acne vulgaris, Chlamydia trachomatis, Q fever, Malaria prophylaxis.

monitoringAdvice: Advise on sun protection; monitor for dysphagia/retrosternal pain.

name: Duodart (Dutasteride / Tamsulosin hydrochloride) 500 mcg / 400 mcg Hard Capsule
indication: Moderate to severe symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) in men with enlarged prostates.
mechanismOfAction: Dutasteride dual-inhibits type 1 and type 2 5-alpha-reductase, suppressing DHT production and shrinking prostate volume; Tamsulosin rapidly relaxes prostatic and bladder neck smooth muscle.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Authority Required (Streamlined) for BPH in patients with an enlarged prostate (prostate volume >= 30 cc or PSA >= 1.5 ng/mL).
counselingAdvice: Take ONCE DAILY approximately 30 minutes after the same meal each day. Swallow capsule whole—do NOT open or chew (liquid contact can cause severe oropharyngeal mucosal irritation). Women who are pregnant or planning pregnancy must NOT handle leaking capsules (teratogenic to male foetus).
cautionsAndContraindications: Category X teratogen for male foetus. Halves serum PSA levels at 6 months—double measured PSA when screening for prostate cancer. Blood donation deferral for 6 months after cessation.
adverseEffects: Impotence/erectile dysfunction, decreased libido, ejaculation disorders, breast tenderness/gynaecomastia, dizziness.
monitoringAdvice: PSA (multiply measured value by 2 after 6 months of therapy to assess true baseline); DRE.

name: Dymista 137/50 (Azelastine hydrochloride / Fluticasone propionate) 137 mcg / 50 mcg per spray (120 sprays) Nasal Spray Suspension
indication: Relief of symptoms of moderate-to-severe seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis/rhinosinusitis not adequately controlled with monotherapy.

name: Estradot (Estradiol (as hemihydrate)) 100 mcg / 24h Transdermal Patch
indication: Hormone replacement therapy for oestrogen deficiency symptoms in postmenopausal women; Prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis.
mechanismOfAction: Replaces declining endogenous 17-beta-oestradiol, alleviating vasomotor symptoms (hot flushes, night sweats) and preventing bone mineral loss. Transdermal route avoids hepatic first-pass metabolism, with lower VTE risk than oral oestrogens.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit for menopausal hormone replacement therapy.
counselingAdvice: Apply to clean, dry, intact skin on lower abdomen or buttocks. Replace patch TWICE WEEKLY (every 3 to 4 days, e.g. Monday and Thursday). Rotate application sites. Never apply on or near breasts. If woman has an intact uterus, a progestogen (e.g. Prometrium) MUST be co-prescribed to prevent endometrial cancer.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in known or suspected breast cancer, oestrogen-dependent neoplasia, active or recent VTE, active arterial thromboembolic disease, undiagnosed abnormal vaginal bleeding. In women with intact uterus, unopposed oestrogen is contraindicated.
adverseEffects: Application site irritation/erythema, breast tenderness, headache, breakthrough spotting, nausea.
monitoringAdvice: Mammography and regular clinical review; investigate any unscheduled bleeding.

name: Imigran (Sumatriptan (as succinate)) 100 mg Film-coated Tablet
indication: Acute relief of migraine attacks with or without aura in adults.
mechanismOfAction: Selective agonist at vascular 5-HT1B and 5-HT1D receptors, causing selective cranial vasoconstriction and inhibiting trigeminal sensory nerve peptide release.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Restricted benefit for acute migraine attacks where standard analgesics fail.
counselingAdvice: Take ONE tablet at the FIRST SIGN of a migraine headache. If no relief is obtained, do NOT take a second dose for the same attack. If headache initially resolves then recurs, a second dose may be taken after at least 2 hours. Max 300mg in 24 hours.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in ischaemic heart disease, coronary vasospasm (Prinzmetal's angina), history of stroke/TIA, uncontrolled hypertension. Allow 24 hours between ergotamines and triptans.
adverseEffects: Sensations of tingling, heat, heaviness, tightness or pressure in any part of the body (including chest/throat), flushing, dizziness, drowsiness, nausea.
monitoringAdvice: Cardiovascular evaluation prior to initiation in patients with cardiovascular risk factors.

name: Jardiance (Empagliflozin) 25 mg Film-coated Tablet
indication: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, Heart failure with reduced or preserved ejection fraction (HFrEF/HFpEF), Chronic kidney disease (CKD).

counselingAdvice: Take once daily in the morning with or without food. Maintain adequate daily fluid intake. Practice good genital hygiene to prevent thrush. Hold medication ('Sick Day Rule') during acute illness, fasting, or prior to major surgery to prevent Euglycaemic DKA.

monitoringAdvice: Renal function (eGFR), volume status, urine ketones if unwell.

name: Lanoxin (Digoxin) 250mcg Tablet
indication: Control of rapid ventricular response in atrial fibrillation/flutter; adjunctive treatment in symptomatic heart failure.
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits cardiac membrane Na+/K+ ATPase, increasing intracellular calcium and inotropy, and stimulates vagal tone to slow AV nodal conduction.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised: Atrial fibrillation rate control and heart failure.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily at the same time. Promptly report nausea, vomiting, yellow-green visual halos, or slow heart rate.
cautionsAndContraindications: Narrow therapeutic index! High risk of toxicity in hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, and renal impairment. Multiple drug interactions (amiodarone, verapamil).
adverseEffects: Nausea, anorexia, visual disturbances (xanthopsia), arrhythmias, bradycardia, confusion.
monitoringAdvice: Serum digoxin levels (target 0.5-0.9 ng/mL for HF; trough drawn >6h post-dose), serum potassium, creatinine/eGFR.

name: Levlen ED (Levonorgestrel / Ethinylestradiol) 150 mcg / 30 mcg (28 day pack) Tablet
indication: Oral contraception, Control of menstrual cycle irregularity, Dysmenorrhoea.
mechanismOfAction: Suppresses pituitary gonadotropins (LH and FSH), preventing ovulation, increasing cervical mucus viscosity, and altering endometrium to impede implantation.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit for contraception and cycle control.
counselingAdvice: Take ONE tablet daily at the same time each day for 28 consecutive days in the order directed on blister. Follow the 'Missed Pill Rule': If a hormone pill is missed by >24 hours, take the missed pill immediately and use barrier contraception (condoms) for 7 consecutive days.

adverseEffects: Breakthrough bleeding, nausea, breast tenderness, headache, weight change, mood changes.
monitoringAdvice: Annual blood pressure measurement and cervical screening.

indication: Management of clinical conditions indicated for Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI) (Gastrointestinal).

name: Maxolon (Metoclopramide hydrochloride) 10 mg Tablet
indication: Relief of nausea and vomiting, Gastro-oesophageal reflux, Diabetic gastroparesis.
mechanismOfAction: Antagonises dopamine D2 receptors centrally in the chemoreceptor trigger zone and peripherally, stimulating upper gastrointestinal tract motility.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit for nausea and gastrointestinal motility disorders.
counselingAdvice: Take 10 to 15 minutes before meals. Limit use to a maximum of 5 consecutive days to prevent involuntary muscle twitching or spasms.
cautionsAndContraindications: Black box warning: Risk of extrapyramidal reactions (acute dystonia, oculogyric crisis) especially in young adults (<30 years) and children, and irreversible tardive dyskinesia with prolonged use (>12 weeks).
adverseEffects: Restlessness, drowsiness, fatigue, acute dystonic reactions (facial spasms, trismus), hyperprolactinaemia.
monitoringAdvice: Limit therapy duration to <=5 days. Monitor for abnormal involuntary movements.

name: Methoblastin (Methotrexate) 10 mg Tablet
indication: Severe active rheumatoid arthritis, Severe recalcitrant psoriasis, Psoriatic arthritis.
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) and aminoimidazolecarboxamide ribonucleotide (AICAR) transformylase, leading to extracellular adenosine accumulation and potent anti-inflammatory immunosuppression.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit for Rheumatoid Arthritis and Severe Psoriasis.
counselingAdvice: CRITICAL SAFETY INSTRUCTION: TAKE ONCE WEEKLY ON THE SAME SPECIFIED DAY EACH WEEK (e.g. every Monday). NEVER take daily. Co-prescribe Folic Acid (5mg) taken 24-48 hours after methotrexate to reduce GI and mucosal toxicity. Report dry persistent cough, breathlessness, or fever immediately (methotrexate pneumonitis).
cautionsAndContraindications: BLACK BOX WARNING: Fatal toxicities reported with accidental daily administration. Contraindicated in pregnancy/lactation, severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min), pre-existing bone marrow suppression, chronic liver disease, alcoholism.
adverseEffects: Nausea, stomatitis, oral ulcers, fatigue, elevated transaminases, bone marrow suppression (leukopenia, thrombocytopenia), interstitial pneumonitis, infection.
monitoringAdvice: FBC, LFTs, and renal function at baseline, every 2-4 weeks initially for 3 months, then every 1-3 months once stable.

indication: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, Chronic weight management in obesity (BMI >= 30 or >= 27 with weight-related comorbidity).
mechanismOfAction: First-in-class dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and GLP-1 receptor agonist, enhancing first- and second-phase insulin secretion and significantly reducing food intake.
pbsRestrictionNote: Non-PBS / Private Prescription in Australia for Type 2 Diabetes and chronic weight management.
counselingAdvice: Inject once weekly subcutaneously. Rotate injection sites. Advise women on oral contraceptives to switch to non-oral barrier methods for 4 weeks after initiation and after each dose escalation due to delayed gastric emptying.
cautionsAndContraindications: History of pancreatitis, severe gastroparesis, medullary thyroid carcinoma. Not recommended in severe gastrointestinal disease.
adverseEffects: Nausea, diarrhoea, decreased appetite, vomiting, constipation, dyspepsia, abdominal pain.
monitoringAdvice: HbA1c, weight, signs of pancreatitis or gallbladder disease.
storageAdvice: Store in refrigerator (2°C to 8°C). Can be stored at room temperature up to 30°C for up to 21 days.

name: Nexium (Esomeprazole (as magnesium trihydrate)) 20 mg Enteric-coated Tablet
indication: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD), Healing and prevention of NSAID-associated gastric ulcers, Eradication of H. pylori (with antibiotics), Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
mechanismOfAction: S-isomer of omeprazole that irreversibly inhibits the H+/K+-ATPase enzyme system (proton pump) in gastric parietal cells, suppressing both basal and stimulated gastric acid secretion.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Restricted benefit for severe refractory GORD, peptic ulcer, and gastroprotection with NSAIDs.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily in the morning at least 30 minutes before food (swallow whole with water; do not crush or chew). Limit treatment duration to lowest effective dose.
cautionsAndContraindications: May reduce absorption of vitamin B12, iron, and calcium with long-term use. Associated with increased risk of Clostridioides difficile infection, hypomagnesaemia, and osteoporotic bone fractures.
adverseEffects: Headache, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, flatulence, nausea/vomiting, constipation.
monitoringAdvice: Re-evaluate need for continued therapy at 4-8 weeks. Check serum magnesium if on long-term therapy.

indication: Short-term treatment of insomnia (severe or disabling).
mechanismOfAction: Enhances GABA-mediated inhibition at subcortical levels producing sedation, hypnosis, and muscle relaxation.

indication: Management of clinical conditions indicated for Partial Opioid Agonist (S8 Controlled) (Analgesia / Pain).
mechanismOfAction: Mu-opioid receptor agonist; produces analgesia, sedation, and alters emotional perception of pain via central nervous system opioid receptors.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Authority Required: Severe disabling chronic or acute pain unresponsive to non-opioid analgesia.
counselingAdvice: This is a controlled medicine. Take strictly as directed. Avoid alcohol and sedatives. May cause drowsiness; do not drive until effects are known. Prevent constipation with aperients.
cautionsAndContraindications: High risk of tolerance, physical dependence, addiction, and fatal respiratory depression. SafeScript check mandatory in participating Australian states.
adverseEffects: Constipation, nausea, sedation, dizziness, respiratory depression, pruritus, confusion.
monitoringAdvice: Pain score, sedation score, bowel function, SafeScript / ScriptCheck dispensing history.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in secure locked location.

name: Norspan (Buprenorphine) 10mcg / hour Transdermal patch (7-day)
indication: Chronic moderate-to-severe disabling pain unresponsive to non-narcotic analgesia, providing continuous 7-day analgesic coverage.
mechanismOfAction: Partial agonist at mu-opioid receptors and antagonist at kappa-opioid receptors with high receptor affinity and slow dissociation rate.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Authority: Severe chronic pain not responding to non-opioid analgesics.
counselingAdvice: Apply patch to clean, dry, hairless skin on upper outer arm, upper chest, or upper back. Leave on for 7 full days. Rotate patch sites; do not use the same site for 3-4 weeks. Do not expose patch to external heat (heat packs, electric blankets, hot tubs).
cautionsAndContraindications: SafeScript monitored medicine. Respiratory depression risk. Avoid applying heat sources directly over patch as absorption accelerates dangerously.
adverseEffects: Application site erythema, pruritus, sedation, dizziness, constipation, nausea, headache.
monitoringAdvice: SafeScript database, skin integrity at patch removal sites, cognitive status.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in secure locked drug safe.

indication: Management of clinical conditions indicated for Calcium Channel Blocker (DHP) (Cardiovascular).
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle and cardiac myocytes, causing peripheral vasodilation and reducing peripheral resistance.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for hypertension and chronic stable angina.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily. Avoid grapefruit juice which can significantly increase drug concentrations. Fluid retention in the ankles may occur.
cautionsAndContraindications: Caution in severe aortic stenosis and severe hepatic impairment. Non-DHP CCBs contraindicated in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
adverseEffects: Peripheral ankle oedema, flushing, headache, dizziness, gingival hyperplasia.
monitoringAdvice: Blood pressure response, heart rate, signs of dependent peripheral oedema.

mechanismOfAction: Inhibits transmembrane influx of calcium ions into vascular smooth muscle and cardiac muscle, resulting in arterial vasodilation.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit for hypertension and angina.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily with or without food. Can cause swollen ankles (peripheral oedema) especially at higher doses (10mg). Avoid grapefruit juice in large quantities.

adverseEffects: Peripheral oedema (ankles/feet), flushing, palpitations, headache, fatigue, dizziness, gingival hyperplasia (rare).
monitoringAdvice: Blood pressure and assess for peripheral ankle oedema at follow-up.

name: Oratane (Isotretinoin) 10 mg Soft Capsule
indication: Severe cystic, nodular, or conglobate acne; Acne unresponsive to extended courses of oral antibacterials.
mechanismOfAction: 13-cis-retinoic acid that dramatically reduces sebaceous gland size, inhibits sebaceous gland activity, normalises follicular keratinisation, and reduces P. acnes bacteria.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Authority Required strictly for severe cystic acne unresponsive to conventional therapy (prescribed by or in consultation with a dermatologist).
counselingAdvice: BLACK BOX WARNING: HIGHLY TERATOGENIC (Category X). MUST use TWO effective forms of contraception starting 1 month before, during, and 1 month after therapy. adverseEffects: Cheilitis (dry cracked lips in >90%), xerosis, epistaxis, conjunctivitis, elevated triglycerides/cholesterol, elevated transaminases, mood changes/depression (rare), arthralgia.
monitoringAdvice: Baseline and monthly fasting lipid profile, LFTs, and negative serum/urine pregnancy tests in females.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in original blister pack to protect from light and moisture.

name: Oroxine (Levothyroxine sodium) 100 mcg Tablet
indication: Hypothyroidism (primary, secondary, or tertiary), TSH suppression in thyroid cancer.
mechanismOfAction: Synthetic L-thyroxine (T4) converted in peripheral tissues to triiodothyronine (T3), binding to thyroid receptors in cell nuclei to regulate metabolism, growth, and development.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily in the morning on an empty stomach at least 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast with a full glass of water. Do NOT take iron, calcium supplements, or antacids within 4 hours. Keep Oroxine refrigerated (2-8°C); protect from light and moisture.
cautionsAndContraindications: Caution in elderly patients and those with coronary artery disease (start at 25mcg and titrate slowly). Untreated adrenal insufficiency must be treated prior to levothyroxine.
adverseEffects: Symptoms of hyperthyroidism if over-replaced (tachycardia, palpitations, tremor, weight loss, heat intolerance, anxiety, insomnia, osteoporosis).
monitoringAdvice: Serum TSH 6 to 8 weeks after starting or altering dose. Once stable, monitor TSH annually.
storageAdvice: Store refrigerated (2°C to 8°C). Protect from light and moisture.

name: Panafcortelone (Prednisolone) 1 mg Tablet
indication: Severe acute inflammatory conditions (asthma/COPD exacerbations, gout, acute allergic reactions), Autoimmune diseases (rheumatoid arthritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, giant cell arteritis, IBD).
mechanismOfAction: Synthetic adrenocortical steroid with predominantly glucocorticoid properties; binds intracellular glucocorticoid receptors, down-regulating pro-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and inflammatory enzymes.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit.
counselingAdvice: Take as a SINGLE DOSE IN THE MORNING with breakfast to mimic the natural circadian cortisol peak and prevent insomnia. Do NOT stop taking abruptly if you have been on treatment for more than 2-3 weeks (requires gradual tapering to allow adrenal axis recovery).
cautionsAndContraindications: Adrenal suppression with prolonged use (>3 weeks). May mask signs of infection. Increases blood glucose in diabetics. Osteoporosis with long-term therapy (co-prescribe calcium/vitamin D). Peptic ulceration when combined with NSAIDs.
adverseEffects: Insomnia, mood changes, increased appetite, weight gain, hyperglycaemia, fluid retention, hypertension, Cushingoid facies, osteoporosis, skin bruising.
monitoringAdvice: Blood glucose, blood pressure, weight, bone mineral density in long-term treatment.

indication: Management of clinical conditions indicated for ACE inhibitor (Cardiovascular).
mechanismOfAction: Competitively inhibits Angiotensin Converting Enzyme (ACE), preventing conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, reducing vasoconstriction and aldosterone secretion.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for hypertension, heart failure, and diabetic nephropathy.
counselingAdvice: Take at the same time each day. May cause dizziness when standing up; rise slowly. Report dry persistent cough or swelling of lips/tongue immediately.

monitoringAdvice: Serum creatinine, eGFR, and electrolytes (potassium) at baseline and 1-2 weeks post-initiation or dose increase.
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C in a dry place.

monitoringAdvice: Baseline LFTs, lipid profile at 6-12 weeks post-initiation or dose change, baseline CK (repeat if muscle symptoms develop).
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C or 30°C in original container protected from moisture.

pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised: Parkinson's disease and symptomatic parkinsonism.
counselingAdvice: Take 30 minutes before meals or 1-2 hours after meals for best absorption. Avoid high-protein meals at time of dosing as amino acids compete for gut and blood-brain barrier transport.

adverseEffects: Nausea, dyskinesias (involuntary movements), orthostatic hypotension, vivid dreams, somnolence.
monitoringAdvice: Motor fluctuations, on-off phenomena, dyskinesias, blood pressure, psychological evaluation.

indication: Management of clinical conditions indicated for Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI) (Gastrointestinal).
mechanismOfAction: Irreversibly inhibits the gastric parietal cell H+/K+ ATPase pump, profoundly suppressing both basal and stimulated gastric acid secretion.

name: Valtrex (Valaciclovir (as hydrochloride)) 1000 mg Film-coated Tablet

indication: Treatment of erectile dysfunction in adult men.

indication: Management of clinical conditions indicated for Statin (Cardiovascular).

pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for hypercholesterolaemia or high cardiovascular disease risk score.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily, with or without food. Statins with short half-lives (simvastatin, pravastatin) are best taken in the evening. Promptly report any unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or brown urine.
cautionsAndContraindications: Contraindicated in active liver disease or unexplained persistent transaminase elevations. Caution in elderly, high alcohol intake, and renal impairment.
adverseEffects: Myalgia, mild gastrointestinal upset, transient transaminase elevation. Rare: rhabdomyolysis, autoimmune necrotizing myopathy.
monitoringAdvice: Baseline LFTs, lipid profile at 6-12 weeks post-initiation or dose change, baseline CK (repeat if muscle symptoms develop).
storageAdvice: Store below 25°C or 30°C in original container protected from moisture.

name: Zofran Zydis (Ondansetron) 4 mg wafer Orally Disintegrating Wafer
indication: Prevention and treatment of nausea and vomiting induced by cytotoxic chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and post-operative nausea/vomiting.
mechanismOfAction: Potent, highly selective 5-HT3 receptor antagonist, blocking serotonin receptors centrally in the chemoreceptor trigger zone and peripherally on vagal nerve terminals.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Restricted benefit for nausea and vomiting associated with cancer chemotherapy or radiotherapy.
counselingAdvice: Place wafer on the tongue; it will dissolve in seconds and can be swallowed with saliva without water. Does not cause drowsiness like older antiemetics.
cautionsAndContraindications: Dose-dependent QT prolongation. Avoid in congenital long QT syndrome. Caution with other QT-prolonging agents. May cause marked constipation.
adverseEffects: Headache (very common), constipation, sensation of warmth or flushing, transient asymptomatic transaminase increases.
monitoringAdvice: Bowel function, ECG if risk factors for QT prolongation.
storageAdvice: Store below 30°C in original foil blister pack.

name: Zoloft (Sertraline (as hydrochloride)) 100 mg Film-coated Tablet
indication: Major depressive disorder, Panic disorder, Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), Social anxiety disorder.
mechanismOfAction: Potent and selective inhibitor of neuronal serotonin (5-HT) reuptake with minimal effect on noradrenaline and dopamine reuptake.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit for Major Depressive Episode, OCD, Panic Disorder, PTSD, and Social Anxiety.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily in the morning or evening with food. Therapeutic effect may take 2 to 4 weeks to develop. Do not cease suddenly due to discontinuation symptoms (dizziness, electric shock sensations).
cautionsAndContraindications: Black box warning: Monitor young adults (<25 years) for worsening depression or suicidal ideation during first weeks. Contraindicated with MAOIs (allow 14-day washout). Caution with other serotonergic agents (tramadol, triptans, St John's Wort).
adverseEffects: Nausea, diarrhoea/loose stools (most frequent SSRI for GI side effects), insomnia, sexual dysfunction (delayed ejaculation, anorgasmia), tremor, dry mouth, hyponatraemia in elderly.
monitoringAdvice: Suicide risk assessment at 1-2 weeks. Monitor sodium in elderly patients.

indication: Management of clinical conditions indicated for Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitor (Rheumatology / Gout).
mechanismOfAction: Inhibits xanthine oxidase (allopurinol) to decrease uric acid synthesis, or impairs leukocyte chemotaxis (colchicine) to suppress crystal-induced inflammation.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS Subsidised for chronic hyperuricaemia and recurrent gouty arthritis.
counselingAdvice: Allopurinol: take after food with plenty of water. Maintain flare prophylaxis (colchicine or NSAID) during initial 3-6 months. Discontinue and call doctor immediately if rash develops.
cautionsAndContraindications: Risk of severe allopurinol hypersensitivity syndrome (DRESS/SJS). Colchicine dose must be strictly reduced in renal/hepatic impairment.
adverseEffects: Rash, GI distress, diarrhoea (colchicine), transaminase elevation. Rare: Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
monitoringAdvice: Serum urate (target < 0.36 mmol/L or < 0.30 mmol/L in tophaceous gout), renal function, LFTs, FBC.

name: Zyloprim (Allopurinol) 100 mg Tablet
indication: Treatment and prevention of chronic gout, Urate nephropathy, Prevention of uric acid nephropathy during cancer chemotherapy.
mechanismOfAction: Purine analogue that competitively inhibits xanthine oxidase, the enzyme responsible for the conversion of hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid.
pbsRestrictionNote: PBS General benefit for hyperuricaemia and gout.
counselingAdvice: Take once daily after food with plenty of water. Co-prescribe anti-inflammatory flare prophylaxis (colchicine 500mcg daily or low-dose NSAID) for the first 3-6 months. Do NOT stop allopurinol if an acute gout flare occurs during treatment.
cautionsAndContraindications: Allopurinol Hypersensitivity Syndrome (AHS / DRESS / Stevens-Johnson Syndrome)—discontinue IMMEDIATELY at the first appearance of skin rash or fever. HLA-B*58:01 allele associated with high AHS risk in Han Chinese, Korean, and Thai ancestry. Reduce dose in renal impairment.
adverseEffects: Maculopapular rash, pruritus, GI upset. Rare: Allopurinol Hypersensitivity Syndrome (severe exfoliative rash, hepatitis, renal failure, eosinophilia).
monitoringAdvice: Serum urate levels (titrate to target < 0.36 mmol/L or < 0.30 mmol/L in tophaceous gout). LFTs and eGFR.
